I genuinely cannot describe how appalling my experience with Ministry of Design has been.

In July 2024, we paid MOD thousands of dollars upfront to redesign and rebuild our website, along with additional work on another online project. We were given timelines and assurances about what would be delivered, but what followed was months of missed deadlines, broken promises and incredibly poor communication.

The most frustrating part is that the website we paid for was never actually built or delivered.

For weeks I repeatedly chased updates through Basecamp, emails and phone calls. Calls regularly went unanswered, messages weren’t returned, and promised updates or meetings simply didn’t happen. Eventually we were shown what I can only describe as an embarrassing prototype that appeared to have had very little time or effort put into it and was nowhere near what we had paid for.

We finally reached the point where we had completely lost confidence in MOD and asked to terminate the project and have our money refunded. Despite the website never being delivered, we did not receive our money back.

Unfortunately, our experience with their hosting and ongoing support has been just as frustrating. Support tickets can take weeks to be dealt with, or often completely ignored. Getting someone on the phone is impossible, messages are regularly left without a callback, and we have had ongoing issues that have impacted the operation of our website and other systems connected to it.

After giving them chance after chance, we have finally moved our hosting elsewhere and ended our relationship with MOD.

I don't leave reviews like this lightly, particularly for another small business, but our experience has been unacceptable.

Based on everything we experienced, I have absolutely no confidence in MOD's ability to design, build, maintain or troubleshoot a website to a professional standard. Their hosting support was, in our experience, virtually non-existent.

I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere for website development or hosting. I certainly would not use MOD again.

I purchased a used Ford Ranger from Regent Kingsley in June 2026. The vehicle was advertised as having a full-service history and being fully workshop tested before sale.

Soon after purchasing it, I took the Ranger to a well-regarded independent Ford specialist for upgrades. Despite the service book showing a service at approximately 116,000 km by Regent Kingsley, the workshop inspected it at around 118,000 km and questioned whether an appropriate service had been completed.

They found a heavily clogged air filter, a very dirty cabin filter, front brakes they considered unroadworthy, and several other maintenance items that I would have expected to be identified during a “fully workshop tested” inspection.

I paid for a full service and raised my concerns with Regent, providing photographs, invoices and feedback from the independent workshop. Duty of Care Manager Jayden Grey was professional, helpful and took my concerns seriously.

Regent’s position was that the vehicle met legal requirements when sold and that the issues related to its previous history rather than work completed by Regent. To their credit, they offered to reimburse the cost of the front brakes, rotors, air filter and cabin filter as a goodwill gesture, which I appreciated and ultimately accepted.

My main disappointment was the communication from Service Manager Jason Rosenwald. Despite leaving several messages, I did not receive a return call and instead received what felt like generic email responses. Something that may have been resolved through a short conversation became more than a week of emails.

Regent later provided an invoice confirming that a standard oil service had been completed. However, I remain unconvinced that the vehicle’s overall condition reflected what most customers would reasonably understand by “full-service history” and “fully workshop tested.”

I asked Regent(Jason) to consider contributing towards some of the additional servicing I had to arrange shortly after purchase, including the fuel filter, transfer case oil, engine oil and oil filter, together with the associated labour. Regent advised that its original goodwill offer was the full extent of what it was prepared to contribute.

I ultimately accepted the reimbursement because I did not want the issue to drag on through further emails back and forth, particularly after being unable to speak with Jason directly despite leaving several messages. My acceptance does not mean my concerns were fully resolved. I still hope someone within Regent’s senior management reviews the matter independently and applies some common sense to the condition in which the vehicle was sold and the costs I incurred shortly after purchase.

While there were positives—particularly Jayden’s assistance and the reimbursement offered—the overall experience has changed my confidence in Regent’s used-vehicle inspection process. I also intend to raise my concerns through the appropriate consumer protection channels as there are issues that still remain to be addressed.

Based on my experience, I strongly recommend arranging an independent pre-purchase inspection, regardless of any advertised service history or workshop checks.

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience with The Yard.

My body corporate hired this company to remove a tree from our communal car park area. I came out at around 2pm to leave for work, shortly after the arborists had left, and discovered that my car had been significantly damaged. This damage was not present when I arrived home and parked my car 10pm the night before. There were scratches across almost the entire vehicle, including the entire right hand side, roof, bonnet, boot, back headlight and rear right window. In fact, every panel except those on the left-hand side appeared to have sustained damage. The damage (pictured) looks like it was caused by tree limbs being dragged over my car.

I initially contacted my body corporate, as they had booked The Yard services. I was informed that my real estate agent had failed to pass on a message from the body corporate advising me to move my car before the works commenced.

I contacted The Yard Services via email to hopefully reach a resolution. I received no response, so I called the company.

Unfortunately, the man who answered the phone spoke to me in an abhorrent, incredibly rude and unprofessional manner and would not allow me to properly explain what had happened. I was repeatedly interrupted, spoken over and berated throughout the conversation.

The first thing he said to me was, “We weren’t even working anywhere near your car.”

I explained that this was exactly why I was confused. The tree was a reasonable distance from where my car had been parked (see images), and I was trying to understand how the team could have caused such extensive damage. From what I could see, it appeared that branches or sections of the tree may have been dragged from the work site past my car, presumably towards their vehicle.

He then responded, “Yeah, well, we told everyone to move their cars.”

I clarified that I had not received this message. He mockingly asked me, “Do you have video evidence of us causing damage to your car?” When I challenged this response and attempted to continue the conversation, he abruptly hung up on me.

Regardless of the miscommunication between the real estate agent, body corporate, tenants and tradespeople, the way this situation was handled was horrendous. It does not excuse the condition in which I found my car, nor does it excuse the way my concerns were dismissed and mocked when I attempted to raise them.

There was no note left on my vehicle acknowledging the damage, no attempt by the company to contact me, and my own attempts to contact them were initially ignored and ultimately dismissed. Most disappointing of all was being treated with complete disrespect when I was simply trying to discuss significant damage to my property.

The extent of the scratches was substantial and, given how many panels were affected, honestly looked almost unbelievable. I was left feeling completely disregarded over something that was not my fault.

The worst part, the tree stump left behind looks like it was hacked apart by seagulls…

Based on the damage to my vehicle and, more importantly, the way my concerns were handled, I would not recommend The Yard Services. I would expect a professional company to take responsibility for investigating a legitimate concern and, at the very least, treat a query with basic courtesy and respect.

When I arrived to collect my vehicle, the first car I was allocated had not been cleaned, as confirmed by the staff member at the counter. I was then given another vehicle, but it did not have a full tank of fuel, so I had to wait while it was filled.

Once I drove away, I immediately noticed an extremely strong, foul and persistent odour inside the vehicle. The smell was so unpleasant that it made the car difficult to remain in comfortably. I initially hoped it would disappear after airing the vehicle out, but even after driving approximately 25 minutes home with the windows open, the overpowering smell remained.

What was particularly concerning was that the odour appeared to be embedded throughout the vehicle, including on the seatbelt and inside the cabin. To me, the smell was similar to the strong personal odour of someone who may have recently been inside the vehicle, such as an employee who had cleaned, fuelled or otherwise prepared the vehicle. I cannot say with certainty what caused the smell, but it was clearly present throughout the vehicle and did not dissipate despite airing it out.

The odour was so bad that I did not feel comfortable continuing to use the vehicle. I contacted customer service straight away and explained how severe the smell was. I was told that I could not return the vehicle that day because the branch had closed. I asked whether another branch was open so I could return it immediately, but I was told there was not. I was advised to return the vehicle the following morning because the vehicle was considered unsatisfactory, and I was told that I would receive a full refund.

I did not drive the vehicle any further and left it parked overnight. I returned it to the Smithfield branch the next morning, keeping the windows open during the drive because the odour remained so strong. Once I arrived, I parked the vehicle, turned it off and left the windows open.

Importantly, the staff member at the Smithfield branch was already aware that I was returning the vehicle, as Head Office customer service had contacted him regarding the situation before I arrived. I followed up on the matter first through IDR, which is a formal complaint within the company, and then through AFCA, the Independent Financial Complaints Authority in Australia. The case is still open.

After filing the complaint, I found that I no longer had access to my transfer history and was unable to place a new order. The message “Your identity verification is being reviewed” was also displayed on my profile. I asked the reason for this change in LiveChat, but I did not receive a specific explanation and was only asked to send proof of identity and address.

I don't know if these changes are related to my complaint and I'm not judging. I just expect the transfer status, the exact meaning of "completed", and any restrictions or account reviews to be clearly explained to the customer.

This review is based solely on my personal experience and the final outcome of the complaint is yet to be determined.

If Google allowed zero-star reviews, I would have given ReseCap zero stars.

I urgently needed to send just $50 to help someone I know. Most exchange providers were unable to process such a small amount due to their limitations. A friend recommended ReseCap because I was told they could even process transfers as small as $10.

I contacted their Telegram support, explained my situation, and asked for assistance. From the beginning, the communication felt extremely impersonal and unhelpful. I genuinely felt as though I was communicating with a bot rather than a real support person because my questions were not answered properly and the interaction gave me very little confidence.

I specifically asked them to provide me with bank account details so I could make the payment. They could simply have told me that bank transfer was not available for such a small transaction. Instead, they repeatedly directed me to their website to place the order.

Eventually, I reached the payment stage, where their website asked me to enter my card details so that ReseCap could charge my card directly. At the same time, my computer/browser was showing multiple security-related warnings, which made me extremely uncomfortable.

I do not know whether this payment method is considered normal for their business, but personally I have never experienced an exchange provider asking me to enter my card details so they could directly charge the transaction amount. I contacted their support again to ask about this, but once again I did not receive a clear or reassuring explanation.

In my opinion, it would have been far more professional simply to tell me from the beginning that they could not provide a suitable payment method for my $50 transfer, rather than sending me back and forth between Telegram and their website.

Based on my personal experience, I found ReseCap’s customer service unprofessional and I would not recommend them. The experience I had was very different from what their advertising had led me to expect.
